title: The Listening Smile
premise: Felix Galloway takes a teaching post in the frost-bound town of Hollowmere, where children vanish one per winter and the school keeps a ledger of names no one will explain. When her childhood imaginary friend, Wren, appears on her porch — unchanged after thirty years — Felix is dragged into a bargain older than the town: the frost takes a child each season unless someone 'belongs' enough to be counted instead. As Felix uncovers that her own family helped found the count, she must choose between duty to the town's survival and love for the students she refuses to surrender. In the end, Felix offers herself as the belonging the frost seeks, but Wren — who was never imaginary at all, only the last person the frost released — takes her place, and Felix leads the families out ahead of the final frost pattern, carrying Wren's name home with her.
about_author: Tamsin Blackwood is the pen name of a former rural schoolteacher who spent nine winters in northern mill towns where old bargains are still whispered at hockey rinks and church suppers. She writes horror about institutions that keep ledgers, and the people brave enough to burn them.

chapters.title: The Ledger in the Coatroom
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Arriving in Hollowmere, Felix finds a leather ledger of vanished children tucked behind the coatroom radiator, its last entry dated last winter. The principal, Mrs. Aldous, gently asks her to put it back. Emotional beat: unease dressed as small-town quirk; Felix's rationalism established as armor.

chapters.title: Wren on the Porch
chapters.summary: POV Felix. On her first frost night, Felix opens her door to Wren — her childhood imaginary friend, ageless, patient, delighted. Wren says only: 'You came back to where I could find you.' Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread as memory and present overlap.

chapters.title: Empty Desk, Full Chair
chapters.summary: POV Felix. A student, Ilsa Brandt, stops attending; her desk remains perfectly kept. Classmates say she's 'gone ahead of the count,' and no adult will say what counts. Felix visits the Brandt farm and finds frost patterns on every window shaped like handwriting. Emotional beat: grief denied by a complicit community.

chapters.title: What the Frost Writes
chapters.summary: POV Felix, with an interlude from Wren. Wren explains the bargain obliquely: Hollowmere gives the frost one belonging each winter, and the frost spares the rest. Felix refuses to believe until she photographs the window-script and it rearranges overnight to spell her surname. Emotional beat: skepticism cracking under evidence.

chapters.title: The Founders' Names
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Digging through church archives, Felix learns the Galloways were among the twelve founding families who first offered a child to end a famine winter — and that the count requires a founder's blood when the frost deepens. Her grandmother's signature is on the original covenant. Emotional beat: inheritance as indictment.

chapters.title: Aldous Explains the Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Mrs. Aldous. The principal reveals she lost her own daughter to the count decades ago and has kept the ledger ever since, believing order is mercy. She warns Felix: run, and the frost takes three instead of one. Emotional beat: antagonist-as-tragedy; duty wearing love's face.

chapters.title: The Count Begins
chapters.summary: POV Felix. First snow seals the roads. Children begin sleepwalking toward the treeline, and Wren confesses she was a real girl, taken by the frost two generations ago and let go because no one remembered her — forgetting is the only escape. Emotional beat: terror plus a terrible hope.

chapters.title: Names in the Window
chapters.summary: POV Felix. The frost script now lists every family that will lose a child if the count isn't paid — including Felix's students. She organizes a midnight exodus, but the roads loop back on themselves; the town won't release anyone before the frost writes its final pattern. Emotional beat: love against duty at full pressure.

chapters.title: The Final Pattern
chapters.summary: POV Felix. On solstice night, Felix offers herself at the treeline as a founder's blood, demanding the covenant name her instead of the children. The frost accepts — then Wren steps forward, claiming the count owes her a debt for being forgotten, and trades herself back into the ice so the pattern completes without a child. Emotional beat: sacrifice answered by sacrifice.

chapters.title: Ahead of the Count
chapters.summary: POV Felix. At dawn the roads open. Felix leads the families out past the frozen fields, carrying the ledger to burn rather than continue, while Wren's name — spoken aloud for the first time in eighty years — thaws a single clear patch of glass behind them. Emotional beat: mourning braided with belonging; leaving is surviving.
